questions.question: What should you do to turn right at a red light?

options.text: Slow down and look for traffic before turning.
Stop, signal, then turn when it is safe. Make sure no sign says you cannot turn.
Signal and wait for the light to turn green.
Wait for a green turn arrow before turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, signal, then turn when it is safe. Make sure no sign says you cannot turn.
questions.explanation: At a red light, you can turn right if no sign forbids it. You must come to a complete stop first. Always use your turn signal.

questions.question: What does a double solid yellow line down the center of a two-lane road mean?

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions. Drivers cannot pass.
Traffic moves in opposite directions. Drivers can pass when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction. Drivers cannot pass.
Traffic moves in the same direction. Drivers can pass when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in opposite directions. Drivers cannot pass.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Solid yellow lines mean you cannot pass.

questions.question: What should you do if you stop along the road at night?

options.text: Turn off all lights.
Use only your parking lights.
Use only your headlights.
Turn on emergency flashers and keep your low beam headlights on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on emergency flashers and keep your low beam headlights on.
questions.explanation: When you stop on the road at night, turn on your emergency flashers and low beam headlights. Other drivers need to see your vehicle clearly.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a school bus with its stop arm extended?

options.text: Come to a complete stop and wait.
Honk your horn and pass on the left side.
Keep driving when you think the children are done exiting.
Pass the bus before its door opens.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and wait.
questions.explanation: You must come to a complete stop when a school bus has its stop arm out. Do not go until the stop arm is raised.

questions.question: Which statement is true about driving on wet roads?

options.text: Your tires become less effective as you drive faster.
Water does not affect cars with good tires.
Deep water is safer than shallow water.
The road becomes more slippery as you slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your tires become less effective as you drive faster.
questions.explanation: The faster you drive on wet roads, the less grip your tires have. If you go too fast, your tires lose contact with the road and you hydroplane or slide on water.

questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks can your body process in one hour?

options.text: Half a drink.
One drink.
Two drinks.
Three drinks.

questions.correctAnswerText: One drink.
questions.explanation: Your body eliminates about one drink of alcohol per hour.

questions.question: What must you do when entering a street from a driveway?

options.text: Drive slowly so other vehicles and pedestrians have time to move.
Honk your horn to alert others to give you room.
Stop and only go when no pedestrians or vehicles are coming.
You can ignore pedestrians if there is no sidewalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and only go when no pedestrians or vehicles are coming.
questions.explanation: Always stop before entering the road from a driveway. Yield to all approaching vehicles and pedestrians. You must stop before crossing the sidewalk.

questions.question: If you are stranded in a snowstorm, what should you do?

options.text: Get out of the car and look for help.
Lie down in your car and sleep.
Walk to the road and flag down other drivers.
Stay in your car. You are most likely to be found there.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your car. You are most likely to be found there.
questions.explanation: If you are stranded in a snowstorm, stay in your car and wait for help. You are more likely to be found in your vehicle. It is also unsafe to walk around in heavy snow.

questions.question: What should you always do at a light rail intersection?

options.text: Look both ways before crossing tracks.
Pay attention and follow all traffic signals.
Share the road with pedestrians and bicyclists.
Do all of these.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do all of these.
questions.explanation: Never drive around lowered crossing gates. Look both ways before crossing tracks. Obey all signs and traffic signals. Trains share the road with cars and bicycles.

questions.question: When can you park or stop on a freeway shoulder?

options.text: As long as you turn on your emergency flashers.
If no part of your vehicle is on the road.
If you need to check a map for directions.
Only in an emergency.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only in an emergency.
questions.explanation: You cannot park on a freeway shoulder except in an emergency.

questions.question: To park legally on a street, your vehicle must be within what distance of the curb?

options.text: Six inches of the curb.
12 inches of the curb.
18 inches of the curb.
24 inches of the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: 12 inches of the curb.
questions.explanation: You cannot park more than 12 inches away from the curb.

questions.question: What is the best way to prevent drowsiness on long trips?

options.text: Turn on your car radio.
Slow down.
Stop regularly to rest and stretch.
Move your eyes from side to side while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop regularly to rest and stretch.
questions.explanation: Stop regularly during long trips to rest and stretch. Do this even if you don't feel tired yet.

questions.question: When you turn left onto a one-way street, which lane should you end up in?

options.text: The right lane.
The lane closest to where you came from.
Either lane.
Neither lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to where you came from.
questions.explanation: Turn into the lane that is closest to the lane you were in before. This is the safest way to turn.

questions.question: What does a steady green light mean?

options.text: You must slow down and be ready to stop.
You must stop and check for oncoming traffic.
You may drive through if the road is clear.
You cannot turn right.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may drive through if the road is clear.
questions.explanation: A green light means you can go through the intersection if it is safe. You can turn right or left on a green light unless a sign says you cannot. Always yield to other vehicles and pedestrians.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A community group is picking up trash along the highway.
Workers are on or near the road ahead.
Children are playing ahead.
A pedestrian crosswalk is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Workers are on or near the road ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that workers may be on or very close to the road. Drive carefully through this area.

questions.question: A driver age 21 or older cannot drive if their blood THC level is at least ____ nanograms per milliliter.

options.text: Zero nanograms
One nanogram
Three nanograms
Five nanograms

questions.correctAnswerText: Five nanograms
questions.explanation: Drivers age 21 and older cannot drive with five or more nanograms of THC per milliliter of blood. Drivers under 21 cannot drive with any THC in their blood. Driving under the influence of marijuana is dangerous.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Turn right only after making a complete stop.
Right turns are not allowed.
Left turns are allowed.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right turns are not allowed.
questions.explanation: This is a regulatory sign that shows a law you must follow. This sign means you cannot turn right.

questions.question: When driving in traffic, what is the safest speed?

options.text: Change your speed often to stay alert.
Drive faster than other vehicles.
Drive slower than other vehicles.
Drive at the same speed as traffic around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive at the same speed as traffic around you.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers go faster or slower than other vehicles. Always drive at the same speed as the traffic around you, staying within the speed limit.

questions.question: Is it legal to drive while under the influence of marijuana, even if it was used legally?

options.text: Yes, it is legal.
No, it is illegal.
Yes, but it is not recommended.
Yes, and it is recommended.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, it is illegal.
questions.explanation: Driving under the influence of marijuana is illegal, even if you obtained it legally. Marijuana can affect your sense of space, time, and speed, making driving dangerous.

questions.question: When can you safely pass on a two-lane street?

options.text: When you can clearly see the road ahead.
When you can return to your lane before meeting oncoming cars.
When your vehicle is fast enough to pass.
When all of the above are true.

questions.correctAnswerText: When all of the above are true.
questions.explanation: You can only pass safely on a two-lane street when you can see clearly ahead, return to your lane before oncoming traffic, and your car is fast enough to pass. Never pass where it is illegal or unsafe.

questions.question: What do work zone signs mean?

options.text: It is summer.
You must stop right away and back up.
Driving conditions are not ideal.
You should drive faster to leave the work zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving conditions are not ideal.
questions.explanation: Work zone signs are orange. They tell you that work is happening on or next to the road. Drive carefully when you see these signs.

questions.question: When you need to slow down on a slippery road, what should you do first?

options.text: Press your brakes hard.
Release the gas pedal.
Use your parking brake.
Pump your brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: First, take your foot off the gas pedal. If you need to slow down more, gently press the brake pedal with steady pressure.

questions.question: A car is coming toward you on the left, and a bicycle is on your right. What should you do?

options.text: Pull onto the shoulder.
Go between both of them.
Let the car pass first, then pass the bike.
Pass the bike quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the car pass first, then pass the bike.
questions.explanation: When there are multiple hazards, deal with one at a time. Let the oncoming car pass first. Then pass the bicycle when it is safe.

questions.question: Can you cross a double solid yellow line to pass another car?

options.text: Yes.
No.
Yes, if there is no oncoming traffic.
Yes, if the car ahead is driving below the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: No.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean no one may cross them, except when turning into a driveway or business entrance. Passing is never allowed over a solid yellow line.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lines in the middle of the road mean?

options.text: Railroad crossing ahead.
Pedestrian crossing ahead.
No passing allowed in either direction.
Passing is allowed in either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: No passing allowed in either direction.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean no passing from either side. You may cross them only to turn or to pass pedestrians, bicycles, scooters, or skateboards when the other lane is clear and safe.
